title: Pseudo-Palindromic Paths in a Binary Tree
summary: In a binary tree with node values ranging from 1 to 9, count the paths from the root to leaf nodes where at least one permutation of the node values forms a palindrome.
statement: In a binary tree with node values ranging from 1 to 9, count the paths from the root to leaf nodes where at least one permutation of the node values forms a palindrome.
constraints: Node values are digits one through nine.
Count root-to-leaf paths whose values can be permuted into a palindrome.

At a leaf, a palindrome permutation is possible when at most one count is odd.
A bit mask has at most one set bit exactly when mask & (mask-1) equals zero.
